svg.title: Run One Improvement Experiment: turn a prediction into the next decision
svg.desc: Hypothetical Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle for routine draft review. Plan: test one daily twenty-minute shared review session, predicting useful feedback within one working day for at least eight of ten routine requests; Maya coordinates a two-week trial. Do: three team members try the slot, retain the urgent-review route, and track the first ten eligible requests plus attendance, duration, and support coverage. Study: four of ten prior comparable requests met the one-day target; seven of ten trial requests met it, below the prediction. Median session duration was twenty-six minutes, above the twenty-minute budget, and support coverage clashes occurred. Act: adapt by testing a rotating qualified reviewer, retain the measures, and repeat before wider adoption. Arrows connect plan to do to study to act and back to plan. All results are invented; the small before-and-after comparison does not prove causation.
svg.text: Turn a prediction into the next decision
Hypothetical routine-draft review · Mixed results lead to a revised test
Prediction: at least 8 of 10 routine drafts get
Owner: Maya · Review after two weeks.
Three team members try the shared slot.
Track the first 10 eligible routine requests.
Prior comparable requests: 4 / 10 within a day.
A mixed result, with limited evidence.
Keep the timing and support measures.
Use the result to plan the next cycle.
Mixed evidence can justify a better next test.
All numbers and events are invented. Ten requests and a before-and-after comparison do not prove causation.
The target and duration belong to this example; actual tests need measures and scope suited to their question.
